Aether doesn't delete comments. They remain on the blockchain. Aether is ephemeral, like spoken conversation, though. After 6 months, if a post has received no comments, it goes stale, and is no longer visible. If somebody actually valued that comment, and wanted to keep it on the radar, they could post a comment to it to refresh it for another 6 months. There are a couple of main reasons why Aether is ephemeral: 1) Not having everything you ever say visible forever is quite nice really 2) Technically, it helps the Aether network stay speedy.

If you or others want to archive stuff long term, definitely look at ipfs: https://ipfs.io The easy way to start is use the ipfs-desktop and pin your valued files, and publish them using a sensible name and the ipfs Qm hash. You can see a tool for text sharing using ipfs here:
